name: car_wheels
title: a car's two axles of real rims and tires, tucked into wheel arches on the body's sides.
why: Any car, van, or truck at figure scale: the running gear that makes it read as a road vehicle, its wheels at the body's sides under arches, sized by the width class.
note: How it differs from the rejected wheel_axle and wheel_arch: no 4870 (whose pins hang 3 plates below the plate, so the small 4624 wheels dangled under a flat plate like landing gear). The pins here are flush (4600, or two 4488 for 6 and 8 wide), the wheel is a 14 mm rim with a 21 mm tire (11209, about 2.6 studs across) standing at the body's side, and a mudguard whose arch wraps the tire's top (98282, or the taller 50745 at 8 wide) sits on a 2-wide spine, so the side view is a tire in a wheel well. The holders sit a whole 4 plates up and the wheels ride 0.75 LDU low on their pins (inside the 1 LDU joint tolerance), so the tires touch z and the deck is on the plate grid. Widths 6 and 8 validate too (checked at wheelbase 10 and 12). The exact holders and mudguards in the books were not confirmed part by part.

name: truck_spine_chassis
title: a 6-wide city truck's frame, a 2-wide spine with the axles under it, widened by plates laid across and locked by a keel brick.
why: The base of every 6-wide city truck: a stiff spine with the axles and arches built in, ready for a cab on the front and a bed behind.
note: VARIANT of spliced_chassis: there two wide plates are spliced; here a 2-wide spine carries the axles and plates laid across widen it, with a keel brick over the spine's joint. Uses the same wheel unit as car_wheels at 6 wide; axles=3 gives a tandem rear (the alternate semi_tractor_frame folds in here). Checked at lengths 16, 20, 22, 26.

name: six_wide_truck_cab
title: a city truck's cab for one figure, a full-width windscreen on a dash, side windows, and a roof with a light bar that lifts off.
why: The cab of a city truck, van, or tow truck: one seated figure behind a full-width windscreen, with a roof that lifts off and a light bar.
note: VARIANT that combines cab_seat, light_bar (both called through m.use) and a 6-wide windscreen. The book's doors (1 x 3 x 2 on rails) are left out: their hinges have no connector data; side windows stand in the door bays.

name: cab_over_sleeper
title: a semi-truck's tall sleeper behind its cab, smooth sides built as flat panels stood on side studs, and a rounded roof fairing that lifts off.
why: The tall sleeper and rounded roof fairing behind a semi-truck's cab, the part that makes a tractor unit read as long-haul.
note: Uses the sideways_built_wall_panel method: 1 x 4 side-stud bricks two plates apart give studs 2 studs apart vertically, and a 4 x 4 plate on its side, tiled, is the smooth panel. The book stands its panels on clips and rounds the fairing with 2 x 4 and 1 x 4 curved slopes; here three 4 x 2 curved slopes (93606).

name: racing_scale_base
title: an 8-wide car's low, stiff floor, wheels on short axles through Technic bricks, Technic sills along the cabin, and two seats side by side.
why: The floor of any 8-wide racing-scale replica: low, stiff, wheels at the full track, Technic sills to pin side skirts to, two seats.
note: Wheels are the 18 mm axle-hole rim (55982) and 30 mm low tire (58090) on an axle 8: the book's 8-wide wheels (18976/18977) have no connector data here. Checked at wheelbase 8 to 16.

name: quarter_tile_headlights
title: the slim swept lights of a racing-scale car's nose, clear tiles with a rounded outer corner on brackets facing the front, a grille between them.
why: The slim, swept headlights of a modern 8-wide sports car's nose.
note: VARIANT of headlights (that one is a 4070 headlight brick with a round tile). Here the lights are on brackets with a quarter-round tile whose round corner is outside and on top; the -y tile needs Rot(x=90, z=-90) to turn it in its own plane (Rot applies x first, so a tile on its back can't be spun with x alone: x = 90 or -90 after y = -90 floats it).

name: side_stud_lights
title: a 6-wide truck's front course, square headlights in its corners and a grille between, all on bricks whose studs face the front.
why: The flush front face of a 6-wide truck or van: headlights in the corners and a grille between, no studs showing.
note: Compared with headlights: headlights uses a headlight brick (4070) with a round tile at each end and plain bricks between, so the middle shows brick; this one puts a side-stud brick under every stud and covers the face: square clear tiles at the corners and grille tiles spanning the studs between, so the whole course is flush. It's the front-facing twin of tail_lights. Found while testing: the library's headlights floats its lenses at z=6 (fine at z=1), so four_wide_car builds its lights this way instead.

name: curved_wedge_nose
title: the rounded, sloping nose of a high-speed train, curved slopes rising from headlights on brackets into a curved canopy windscreen.
why: The nose of a modern high-speed or commuter train, a smooth curve from the headlights up through the cab glass.
note: The book uses 4 x 4 curved wedges (45677) and long double-curved wedges; here three curved slopes 4 x 2 (93606) give the rise, and the canopy is the curved windscreen 3 x 6 (62360), which was never made in Trans Black (Trans Light Blue default).

name: tapered_hood_wedges
title: a vintage car's long hood that narrows toward the grille, two wing plates laid side by side with their slanted edges outside, louvers down the middle.
why: The long hood of a 1930s car or vintage truck that narrows toward the radiator.
note: Wing plates 3 x 6 (or 3 x 12) instead of the book's wedges; the 3 x 8 wings (3544/3545) were only made in grays, black, white, and tan, so length 8 isn't offered. The 3 x 6 left wing's body is 2.95 studs across, so it sits 0.05 in to put its studs on the grid.

name: snot_side_skirt
title: a racing-scale car's flush lower sides, long tiles standing on the side studs of the sill course, with a grille tile as the intake at the back end.
why: The smooth lower sides of an 8-wide sports car below the doors, with an intake ahead of the rear wheel.
note: VARIANT of bracket_side_panel (a 2-stud-tall panel on brackets): here one course of side-stud bricks carries tiles on edge and a grille intake, a skirt a brick tall. The book clips its tiles into pins in Technic sill holes; that clip path has no clean connector match here, so the method moved to side studs.

name: rounded_car_end
title: the smooth rounded corners at the end of a loco or passenger car, quarter-round bricks stacked at each corner and a cap of round-corner plates.
why: The rounded end of a passenger car, loco, tram, or bus, so the body doesn't end in square corners.
note: 85080 and the round-corner plate 79491 turn differently: at rot=0 the brick's round side is at +x, +y and the plate's at +x, -y.

name: window_band
title: the long run of windows down a passenger car's or bus's side, windows side by side over a wall with a colored stripe, a plate course over them, and dark posts where the doors go.
why: The long band of windows along a passenger car, tram, or bus, with a stripe under it and posts at the doors.
note: VARIANT of the window band inside train_carriage: this is one side on its own, for any length, with a stripe course and door bays, so buses and trams can use it.

name: shipping_container
title: a 20-foot freight container for a flat wagon, a truck bed, or a port stack, corrugated panel sides on a plate base that lifts off.
why: Cargo for a flat wagon, truck bed, or port stack: a container that lifts off and stacks.
note: Both ends are closed brick walls: the book's door leaves on clips aren't modeled.

name: lift_off_window_cab
title: a shunting loco's cab with glass on all four sides, built as one box with its roof that lifts off the cab floor to put the driver in.
why: The cab of a shunter or small loco: glass on four sides and a roof that come off as one box to seat the driver.
note: Alternate, in place of flat_wagon: the wagon needs bogies, and the bogie, its wheels, and the bogie plate (38339, 38340, 18626) have no connector data here, so they float. VARIANT of lift_off_roof_seat: the whole glass box is the lift-off unit, a submodel. The book's windows are 1 x 6 x 2 train frames; here 1 x 4 x 3 and 1 x 2 x 3 train windows.

name: vintage_chassis
title: the long, narrow frame of a 1930s car, a 2-wide spine with a T across each axle, white-wall wheels, and running boards hung between the wheels.
why: The frame of a 1930s car or vintage fire engine: narrow spine, wheels and fender T's, running boards between the wheels.
note: Combines long_hood_vintage_chassis and running_board. The book's spoked wheels (30155) have no connector data, so white 14 mm rims stand in as white-walls. The fender T's stand two plates up to clear the tires. The book's pinned-on rear module is not modeled.

name: vintage_radiator
title: the tall brass radiator of an early car or fire engine, a gold bracket faced with grille tiles, a gold cap on top, and a brass lamp each side.
why: The face of a vintage car or early fire engine: a tall brass radiator with a filler cap and brass lamps.
note: Combines brass_radiator and chrome_grille_vintage: pass brass="Light Bluish Gray" for a chrome grille.

name: street_cart
title: a food or popcorn cart on four small wheels, a counter with a glass display, and a peaked canopy on four posts.
why: A popcorn, ice cream, or food cart for a street or park scene.
note: The canopy stands on posts of round bricks, not the book's bars, and the wheels are 14 mm rims, not spoked ones (no connector data).

name: four_wide_car
title: a whole small city car for one figure, sized by the 4-wide rules: wheels in arches on a 2-wide spine, a floor, a windscreen with a roof, a seat, and lights front and back.
why: A whole small city car in one call, sized by the 4-wide rules, for a street scene or a starting point to restyle.
note: The books have no 4-wide car: this is built from the width arithmetic (section 3 of the research) with car_wheels' 4-wide running gear. It calls windscreen and tail_lights from the library; its headlights are built inline because the library's headlights floats its lenses at this height.

name: offroad_fender_flare
title: a chunky arch over each wheel that stands half a stud proud of a boxy body's side, set out on jumper plates.
why: The chunky fender flares of an off-roader or rally car, standing half a stud out over each wheel.
note: VARIANT of jumper_offset: jumpers laid across the body's edge carry a 1 x 4 arch half a stud outside the side. The book's exact arch piece wasn't confirmed.

name: glass_box_cab
title: the all-glass operator's cab of a crane, reach stacker, or digger, clear panels on every side of a small plate, a seat inside, and a tiled roof, built apart and set on the machine.
why: The all-glass operator's cab of a crane, reach stacker, or digger, set off to one side of the machine.
note: The book uses corner windscreen panels; here clear panels 1 x 4 x 3 all round. It's a submodel, placed on any studs, so it can hang over the deck's edge (the example) or sit on a bracket.
